title: 1953 AHSME Problem 29
statement: The number of significant digits in the measurement of the side of a square whose computed area is \(1.1025\) square inches to the nearest ten-thousandth of a square inch is:

solutions.text:
The reported area means the true area lies in \[ 1.10245\le A\lt1.10255. \] Taking square roots gives approximately \[ 1.049976\le\sqrt A\lt1.050024. \] Every possible side length therefore rounds to \(1.0500\) to the nearest ten-thousandth. The trailing zeros after the decimal are significant, so \(1.0500\) has five significant digits.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The true area lies from \(1.10245\) up to \(1.10255\) square inches
Take square roots of the error interval and see how many digits of the side are fixed
